title: U.S. House · Alabama's 7th Congressional District
area: Alabama's Black Belt, including western Jefferson County (part of Birmingham), Selma, Tuscaloosa, and much of west-central Alabama; Alabama's only Democratic-leaning and majority-Black district.

context.text: Incumbent Terri Sewell (D) advanced without a primary. Ammie Akin defeated David Perry 73.4% to 26.6% in the August 11, 2026 Republican primary. A new congressional map, signed after the Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling, moved this district's primary from May 19 to August 11, 2026 and reopened the candidate filing deadline, after which two Republicans filed to run (none had filed under the original map). Cook Political Report rated the district D+10 for 2026.

candidates.name: Terri Sewell
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Alabama's 7th Congressional District (since 2011)

summary.text: Terri Sewell is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Alabama's 7th Congressional District, first elected in 2010. Raised in Selma, she is a Harvard-trained public finance lawyer who was the first Black woman partner at Maynard, Cooper & Gale before running for Congress. She is the first Black woman to serve in Alabama's congressional delegation, sits on the Ways and Means and House Administration committees, and is a Chief Deputy Whip in the 119th Congress.

background.text: Born in Huntsville, Alabama, in 1965 and raised in Selma, where she was the first Black valedictorian of Selma High School; her official biography calls her a product of Alabama's rural Black Belt.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Princeton University (1986), studied at the University of Oxford on a Marshall Scholarship (1988), and earned a J.D. from Harvard Law School (1992).
Served as a judicial law clerk to Chief Judge U.W. Clemon of the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Alabama, then worked at the New York firm Davis Polk & Wardwell beginning in 1994.
Returned to Alabama in 2004 and became a public finance lawyer at Maynard, Cooper & Gale in Birmingham, where she was the first Black woman partner.

Ran for the open 7th District seat in 2010 after Rep. Artur Davis left to run for governor; won the Democratic primary runoff over Jefferson County Commissioner Sheila Smoot and the general election with 72.4% of the vote.
Is one of the first women elected to Congress from Alabama in her own right and the first Black woman in the state's congressional delegation; was Freshman Class President in the 112th Congress.
Sits on the Ways and Means Committee (Ranking Member of the Oversight Subcommittee) and the Committee on House Administration (Ranking Member of the Elections Subcommittee).

In the 119th Congress, serves as a Chief Deputy Whip and on the Democratic Steering and Policy Committee; chairs the Congressional Black Caucus Voting Rights Task Force and belongs to the New Democrat Coalition.

priorities.text: Says bringing jobs and opportunities to every corner of the district is her top priority, and runs an annual Job Fair connecting jobseekers and employers.
Says she is leading the fight in Congress to restore the Voting Rights Act of 1965 through the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, which she reintroduced in the 118th Congress.

positions.summary: Says she strongly supports the Affordable Care Act, citing its protections against denial of coverage for pre-existing conditions and caps on out-of-pocket costs.
positions.quote: That is why I strongly support President Obama’s health care plan and the health care reform signed in to law last March.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means (Oversight, Social Security, and Trade subcommittees) and the Committee on House Administration (Elections Subcommittee) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

Served as Ranking Member of the House Administration Committee's Elections Subcommittee and on the House Committee on Armed Services (Military Personnel Subcommittee) in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).

Sponsored the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, reintroduced in the 118th Congress on September 19, 2023, which would restore federal preclearance requirements under the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

candidates.researchNotes: Sewell has not completed a recent Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and no distinct 2026 campaign issues page was found; positions and priorities are drawn from the issue pages on her official House site, some of which have not been updated with dated statements in recent years.

candidates.name: Ammie Akin
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary, 73.4% to 26.6%, over David Perry.

summary.text: Ammie Akin is an educator and entrepreneur running as the Republican nominee for Alabama's 7th Congressional District. Her campaign says she began her career teaching students with special needs in Hoover, holds a doctorate in educational leadership from Samford University, and co-founded what it describes as the country's first "shared" nonprofit facility. She won the August 11, 2026 special Republican primary and lists affordability, rural health care, education, and support for law enforcement among her priorities.

background.text: According to her campaign website, earned degrees from the University of Alabama, and a master's degree and a doctorate in educational leadership from Samford University.

According to her campaign website, began her career about 25 years ago teaching a group of students with special needs in Hoover, and later helped raise funds for and build a campus for a program called Unless U.
Describes a 25-year career in education as a teacher, principal and nonprofit leader, and says she has taught future principals and superintendents at the University of Alabama.

Describes herself as an entrepreneur, multi-level educator and longtime advocate for people with disabilities; co-founded a nonprofit facility that her campaign describes as the first of its kind in the country.

According to her campaign website, she and her husband are developing Hub in the Hills, a privately funded project to turn a former elementary school into a shared campus for nonprofit organizations and programs for adults with disabilities.
Won the August 11, 2026 special Republican primary with 73.4% of the vote over David Perry, a pastor from Selma.

priorities.text: Says she would "put Alabama first" by prioritizing families, workers, small businesses, and local communities over partisan politics.
Says she would fight wasteful Washington spending and demand accountable use of taxpayer dollars.
Says she would work to strengthen rural healthcare access and help keep rural hospitals open.

candidates.researchNotes: Akin has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and has no Ballotpedia biography beyond her campaign profile; her campaign website is limited to brief priority statements with little further detail on specific policy positions.
